propositions: The test_rendered_output_is_byte_identical_to_the_landed_renderer test kills pytest-xdist workers on macOS py3.13 due to exceeding the 300-second per-test timeout when running serially over 884 corpus units with ~1768 pandoc spawns.
Test execution time is load-dependent: 91.6 seconds idle but 504.8 seconds under CPU saturation (1.7x over the 300s guard), causing intermittent failures only on the contended macOS CI lane.

The pytest-timeout thread method calls os._exit(1) from a timer thread, killing the worker outright with no traceback or assertion text, making the failure opaque as a worker crash rather than a test failure.

Chunking the equivalence test into fixed-size batches (parametrized by _EQUIVALENCE_CHUNK=40) bounds per-test cost structurally so corpus growth adds test cases rather than lengthening any single case.
A coverage guard test (test_the_equivalence_chunks_cover_every_renderable_unit) must verify all chunks reassemble to the full _renderable_units list with stride 1 to prevent silent unit omission.
